title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' Grothendieck works with a profinite group G generated by a pair (rho, sigma), called a 'couple modulaire'. The model is PSL2(Ẑ) or SL2(Ẑ), with rho of order 3, sigma of order 2 or 4, and parabolic element eps0 = sigma^{-1} rho. To such a pair he attaches a family of groups:
- Sigma: a group of automorphisms;
- B (normaliser of the cusp group);
- G (the 'outer' group stabilising the relevant conjugacy classes);
- gamma;
- Z_rho and Z_sigma (normalisers of <rho> and <sigma>);
- Gamma, S_0M and M (the analogue of the GT / M_{0,3}^~ type group).
On p.521 he decided to prime all of these notations. He then treated case 2°, G = PSL2(Ẑ), by reference to §48.

This page, case 3°: G = SL2(Ẑ) ('cas complet modulaire'). He lists the primed groups.
- B' = {(mu lambda; 0 1) : mu in Ẑ*, mu ≡ 1 mod 3, lambda in Ẑ}. This is the stabiliser of the cusp: (mu lambda; 0 1) conjugates the unipotent (1 x; 0 1) to (1 mu x; 0 1).
- G' = GL'(2,Ẑ) = {u in GL2(Ẑ) : det u ≡ 1 mod 3}. These are the GL2-conjugations that preserve the SL2-conjugacy class of rho. In SL2(F3) the order-3 elements split into two classes, swapped by det = -1.
- Z'_rho = {c rho + d : c, d in Ẑ, c^2 + cd + d^2 in Ẑ*} = (Ẑ ⊗ Z[zeta_3])*, the centraliser of rho. Its norms are automatically ≡ 1 mod 3, since c^2 + cd + d^2 ≡ (c - d)^2 mod 3. So it lies in GL'.
- Z'_sigma = T'_sigma · {1, tau_inf}, where T'_sigma = (Ẑ ⊗ Z[i])* = {t + sigma u : t^2 + u^2 in Ẑ*} and tau_inf = diag(-1, 1) is the reflection inverting sigma.
- The groups S_0M', M', S_0Gamma' and Gamma' are the Ẑ-points of the group schemes of §48, modulo Sigma_0.

Section III, 'Le groupe M_{rho,sigma}', for a general couple. The construction is:
1. Take the homomorphism (1) Ẑ → G, n ↦ eps0^n, eps0 = sigma^{-1} rho. Its image L_0^G is the procyclic cusp group and its kernel is a closed ideal J.
2. Hence (2) Aut(L_0^G) ≅ (Ẑ/J)*.
3. Conjugation gives (3) B' → Aut L_0^G ≅ (Ẑ/J)*.
4. This factors as a character (4) chi_gamma : gamma' → (Ẑ/J)*.
5. Composing with G' → gamma' gives (4 bis) chi_G : G' → (Ẑ/J)*.

This is the abstract 'cyclotomic character' attached to any modular couple. For G = SL2(Ẑ) one has J = 0 and chi_G = det on GL'(2,Ẑ). For G = π̂1(P^1 − {0,1,∞})-type groups it is the cyclotomic character of GT. For a finite quotient, where eps0 has order N, it lands in (Z/N)*.

The section III draft is struck through with diagonal lines; it is restarted on p.523 with the extension N_{1,1}^~ of M_{0,3}^~ by {±1}.
errors: Z'_sigma = T'_sigma·{1, tau_inf} is not contained in GL'(2,Ẑ) as written. det tau_inf = −1 ≢ 1 mod 3, and units t+sigma·u can have norm ≡ 2 mod 3. The correct normaliser inside G' should be (T'_sigma·{1, tau_inf}) ∩ GL'(2,Ẑ): norm-≡1 elements alone, and norm-≡2 elements times tau_inf. This is a gap or an implicit convention, unlike the rho case, where norms are automatically ≡ 1 mod 3.

B' is given by representatives (mu lambda; 0 1). Since G' = GL'(2,Ẑ) contains the scalars Ẑ* (acting trivially), the actual stabiliser of the cusp in G' is the full upper-triangular subgroup with a/d ≡ 1 mod 3. The listed set is a section modulo scalars; this is harmless for the character but notationally inconsistent.
In (2), (Ẑ*/J)* is a slip for (Ẑ/J)*, as written correctly in (3) and (4).
In (4 bis), G'_rho should be G'_{rho,sigma}.

ideas.what: Explicit description of the normalisers/stabilisers attached to the modular couple in SL2(Ẑ). Centraliser of rho = (Ẑ⊗Z[zeta3])*, normaliser of sigma = (Ẑ⊗Z[i])* extended by a reflection; outer group GL' = {det ≡ 1 mod 3}.
ideas.modern_name: Centralisers of elliptic elements (CM tori) in GL2(Ẑ); outer automorphisms of SL2(Ẑ) preserving the conjugacy classes of torsion
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard folklore (Serre, Trees; modular group theory)

ideas.what: Abstract cyclotomic character chi : G' → (Ẑ/J)*, defined by the action on the procyclic cusp group generated by eps0 = sigma^{-1} rho, for an arbitrary profinite group with a modular couple.
ideas.modern_name: Cyclotomic character of GT; 'virtual cyclotomic character' of GT-shadows / GT-type groups attached to quotients of PSL2(Ẑ) or F̂2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld/Ihara for GT; Dolgushev et al. (GT-shadows, ~2021) for finite-level versions with values in (Z/N)*
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses Gal(Q̄/Q) acting on Teichmüller tower and the cyclotomic character informally; this general version is not published

ideas.what: Uniform family of groups (B, G, gamma, Z_rho, Z_sigma, Gamma, S_0M, M) attached to any 'couple modulaire', specialised to SL2(Ẑ) and PSL2(Ẑ) as test cases.
ideas.modern_name: GT-like groups relative to a quotient of the modular group (Harbater–Schneps; GT-shadows)

missed.claim: For an arbitrary profinite quotient G of the modular group with a modular couple (rho, sigma), Grothendieck defines the character into (Ẑ/J)*, J = ann(eps0), through the cusp normaliser. This is exactly the structure later rediscovered in the theory of GT-shadows (finite-level GT approximations), whose 'virtual cyclotomic character' takes values in (Z/N_ord)*, with N_ord the order of the image of the parabolic generator.
missed.quote: n ↦ ε0^n où ε0 = σ^{-1}ρ (d'image L0^𝔊) et soit J le noyau ... (Ẑ/J)* ≃ Aut(L0^𝔊) ... γ'_{ρ,σ} →χγ (Ẑ/J)*
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Grothendieck had a systematic finite-or-profinite-quotient version of GT with a cyclotomic character, organised around modular couples. Comparing his groups M_{rho,sigma} with GT-shadow groupoids could supply missing structure, such as the Z_rho/Z_sigma normaliser data and the SL2 versus PSL2 extensions.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mostly a notational specialisation to SL2(Ẑ), with routine normaliser computations. The interesting part is the general cyclotomic-type character (Ẑ/J)* attached to any modular couple, which anticipates finite-level GT constructions. However, the idea is natural, and the draft is struck through and restarted on the next page.
transcription_corrections: The S_0M', M', S_0Gamma' lines read 'S₀M'_{ρ,σ} = S₀M'_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ)/Σ₀ avec notation § 48' (S with subscript 0), not a left-subscript script M.
In (2) the manuscript has (Ẑ*/J)*, a slip for (Ẑ/J)*.
(4 bis) reads G'_ρ →χG (Ẑ/J)*, likely intended G'_{ρ,σ}.
The whole section III on this page is crossed out by three diagonal strokes; it is restarted on p.523.
The margin note next to (4) reads 'G'_{ρ,σ} → γ'_{ρ,σ}'.
